confidence_notes: Restaurant anchors draw on several web aggregators and a few venue menus, but sources conflict widely (two-person mid-range figures ranged from about $14 to $50) and many are undated or crowd-sourced. Beer rests on an undated Punta Cana bar menu listing Presidente at $6 and a travel guide citing about $2 for a domestic beer. Coffee rests on a single expat-area cappuccino listing (about RD$360). Cocktail is loosely sourced from budget and upscale guide figures. Wine by the glass has no direct source and is set from the beer relationship. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and the city context; no booking pages or live listings were inspected. The anchors are framed for July 2026, but the source pages are not dated to that month. FX is the RBA 4pm observation for 18 November 2026 as shown on the RBA exchange rates overview page, which a third-party report also gives as 0.6720. Other secondary sources for that date range from 0.6715 to 0.6876. The full F11.1 daily table was not retrieved.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was used. Food and drink anchors are based on Punta Cana's own tourist-zone price data, and accommodation reflects Caribbean resort-area pricing judgement. Cocktail and wine are set relative to the beer anchor because direct local data was weak.
